decks.name: LeetCode #252 - Meeting Rooms
decks.description: Determine if a person can attend all meetings without conflicts

cards.question: Meeting Rooms: Given an array of meeting time intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], determine if a person could attend all meetings.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.explanation: Check every pair of intervals for overlap. For each interval i, compare with all subsequent intervals j. Two intervals overlap if minimum of their ends is greater than maximum of their starts (they share some time). If any overlap found, return false. If all pairs checked without overlap, return true. Simple but inefficient. O(n^2) time checking all pairs.

solutions.timeDescription: Nested loops check all pairs of intervals, resulting in n*(n-1)/2 comparisons which is O(n^2)
solutions.spaceDescription: Only uses constant extra space for loop variables and interval references
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given intervals=[[0,30],[5,10],[15,20]]: Compare [0,30] with [5,10]: min(30,10)=10 > max(0,5)=5, overlap detected. Return false immediately. Person cannot attend all meetings as first and second conflict.

solutions.name: Sorting
solutions.explanation: Sort intervals by start time first. After sorting, only need to check adjacent intervals for overlap. If previous interval's end is greater than current interval's start, they overlap. If we find overlap, return false. Otherwise return true after checking all adjacent pairs. Sorting ensures we process intervals in chronological order. Much more efficient than brute force. O(n log n) time from sorting.
